facts.text: Module-level client configuration is removed in v1. Bare module-level attribute assignments `openai.api_key = ...`, `openai.api_base = ...`, and `openai.organization = ...` no longer configure the client and must be replaced by constructing an explicit client object, e.g. `client = OpenAI(api_key=...)`.

All module-level namespaced call patterns of the form `openai.<Namespace>.create(...)`, and the equivalent `.list(...)` / `.retrieve(...)` calls, are removed in v1. Named examples: `openai.ChatCompletion.create(...)`, `openai.Completion.create(...)`, `openai.Embedding.create(...)`, `openai.Image.create(...)`, `openai.Moderation.create(...)`. These must migrate to client-based calls, e.g. `client.chat.completions.create(...)`.

The `openai.error` submodule is removed. Exception classes formerly there — `openai.error.RateLimitError`, `openai.error.ServiceUnavailableError`, `openai.error.InvalidRequestError`, `openai.error.AuthenticationError`, and others — now live at the top level of the `openai` package (e.g. `openai.RateLimitError`). Any reference to `openai.error.*` must change.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE / non-breaking: response-object access patterns. Reading a response via dict-style (`response['choices']`) or attribute-style (`response.choices`) access are both still valid; the migration does not change this and such sites must not be flagged.

The three changes listed (module-level config attributes, module-level namespaced API calls, and `openai.error` submodule references) are stated to be the ONLY confirmed breaking changes; anything not described in the guide is unaffected.
Affected sites include ones reached indirectly through a repository's own helper functions — call chains must be traced, not just the entry-point file grepped.
